quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
A parked car has someone sitting in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person walking in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian that might move into your lane. If a driver next to you is too close to the car ahead, they may try to cut in front of you. Use your horn when passing a parked car with someone inside, or when passing a pedestrian or cyclist in the street.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Lean their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than normal.
Keep a greater distance between you and other vehicles.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, so your motorcycle will not respond as quickly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always tell your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride on the left side of your lane because:

options.text: The right side might be slippery.
It gives you a better view of the next lane.
Drivers do not expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the car's rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: In a group ride, less experienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from having to rush to keep up and allows more experienced riders behind them to watch out for them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
Lean toward the direction you are turning.
Keep your feet away from the roadway.
Ignore other vehicles on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore other vehicles on the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Keep your feet off the roadway to avoid losing control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn during a crash.
questions.explanation: For the best protection, use a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards, fits snugly, and has no visible damage. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In any portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind. This prevents the other driver from returning to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm with one finger extended, all riders should move into a single-file line.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags or tie them down. Do not pile items high on the back of the seat. High loads raise the center of gravity and affect balance. Always distribute weight equally on both sides.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far right as possible.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving toward the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Moving away may tempt them to return too soon. Stay centered for safety.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when you accelerate?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. When you accelerate, its weight causes it to lag behind due to inertia.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing. This gives you a better view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you move?
questions.explanation: When making a turn, turn only your head to look where you want to go. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections help ensure your motorcycle is safe to ride.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding toward the other vehicle risks a collision. Riding away may tempt them to merge back too soon.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore the weight transfer. It does not affect braking.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.explanation: As the motorcycle's weight shifts to the front tire while braking, gradually increase pressure on the front brake lever.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This lets you react faster to any hazards.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation is good for staying close while keeping safe distance on straight roads.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because passengers can tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal to ride anywhere except the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.
